clue.text: Rubbished chronic type of fireworks

indicators.note: something rubbished is trashed and broken up, so the letters that follow are scrambled into a new order

parts.note: eleven letters taken as written for the shuffle

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a persistently dreary kind of firework display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies letters; the definition is just 'of fireworks', an adjectival phrase like PYROTECHNIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyrotechnics is the craft of making fireworks, so the adjective describes anything relating to that display art.

clue.text: Person easily manipulated to accept right component of cocktail?

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a pawn is someone used by others for their own ends
standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A gullible person is talked into taking a particular ingredient in their drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The cocktail is not a drink but a prawn cocktail, a classic British starter of shellfish in pink sauce; the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: The shellfish is the main ingredient of the seafood starter called a prawn cocktail, so it is one part of that dish.

clue.text: Editor and assistant interrupting revolutionary in the act

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of something, so the first pair sits inside the next word

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary
common abbreviation for editor
a hand is a helper or worker

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor and their helper barge in on a political radical.
explanation.walkthrough: Red is the traditional colour of communism, so a revolutionary is often a red in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To be caught red-handed is idiomatically to be caught while committing the crime.

clue.text: Passionate Dorothy, embracing one bishop after upset

indicators.note: upset means turned over, which in a down clue flips the whole assembly end to end
embracing means holding something within one's arms, so the name wraps around what follows

parts.note: Dot is a short form of the name Dorothy
Roman numeral for one
RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: Dorothy, distraught, throws her arms around a single clergyman in a passionate scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After upset' tells you the turning comes last, once the name has taken in the numeral and the bishop's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrid affair is one full of intense passion and heat, so the word is a strong synonym for passionate.

clue.text: Top article amongst leaders of Conservative Party

indicators.note: amongst means in the middle of others, so this piece is set inside the selected letters
leaders are the ones at the front, so only the opening letters of the following words count

parts.note: the initial letters of the two words
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A senior figure sits among the heads of the Tory party.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap is a lid or covering for the top of something, like a bottle cap.

clue.text: Year away from US city brought about start of television channel?

indicators.note: brought about means placed around, so the shortened city surrounds the single letter
away from signals that this letter departs, leaving the rest of the name behind

parts.note: the largest American city
abbreviation for year

indicators.note: a start is the beginning, so only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A year after leaving New York, someone launched a TV channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove Y from NEW YORK to get NEWORK, then put T inside it. The question mark admits that a network carries channels rather than being one.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcasting network is a chain of stations sharing programmes, loosely a television channel.

clue.text: Free access that's arranged for central beach

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters that follow are reordered

parts.note: twelve letters taken as written for the shuffle

explanation.surface: Unrestricted entry has been organised to the beach in the middle of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Carte blanche, French for a blank sheet, is complete freedom or unrestricted authority to act.

clue.text: Son in possession of the best male toiletry

parts.note: standard abbreviation for son
having means owning or holding
the cream is the finest part, as in cream of the crop

explanation.surface: A boy owns the finest grooming product for men.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaving cream is lathered on before using a razor, a product traditionally sold for men's grooming.

clue.text: Less easy to restrain old obsessive person

indicators.note: restraining something means holding it in, so the comparative word encloses the letter

parts.note: harder means more difficult
abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An obsessive elderly person is getting tougher to control.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarder compulsively accumulates and keeps possessions, a recognised obsessive behaviour.

clue.text: Early religious leader favoured by former queen

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: A founding churchman enjoyed the favour of a past monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Peter, chief of the apostles, is regarded as the first pope and leader of the early church.

clue.text: Agitated man's valid destructive behaviour

indicators.note: agitated means shaken up, so the letters that follow are stirred into a new order

parts.note: nine letters taken as written for the shuffle

explanation.surface: An upset man claims his wrecking spree was justified.
explanation.definitionFit: Vandalism is the deliberate damaging of property, a destructive act named after the Vandals who sacked Rome.

clue.text: Protective gear delivered to religious group — delivered by post?

parts.note: mail is chain armour
a religious order, such as monks or nuns

explanation.surface: Armour is shipped to a community of monks, presumably through the post.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'delivered' only places the armour before the group; the second belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail-order goods are bought from a catalogue and sent to the buyer through the postal service.

clue.text: Individual working with energy

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A single person is toiling vigorously.
explanation.definitionFit: Individual as a noun means a single person or thing, which is one.

clue.text: Aristocrat, oddly, regularly seen as unimportant figure

parts.note: a nob is a toff, someone upper-class

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the preceding word is taken

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of this word

explanation.surface: A peculiar nobleman is routinely regarded as insignificant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like an anagram signal or a word meaning strangely, but its own letters are the source: take the odd ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobody is a person of no importance or status, the opposite of a somebody.

clue.text: Reserved about new library item

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes round the letter that follows

parts.note: booked means reserved in advance
abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone has set aside a newly acquired book from the library.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookend is a support placed at the end of a row of books, so it is found on library shelves.

clue.text: Coin showing delicate line around head of King

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first two pieces wrap the single letter

parts.note: nice can mean fine or subtle, as in a nice distinction
abbreviation for line

indicators.note: the head is the top, so only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A coin bears a fine inscription circling the monarch's portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice in its older sense means precise or delicate, as in a nice point of law.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickel is the American five-cent coin, named after the metal it contains.

clue.text: Awkward Frenchman's left

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the French word for the left side

explanation.surface: A clumsy Frenchman has departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as departed, but it is the direction, as a French speaker would say it.
explanation.definitionFit: English borrowed the French word for left-handed to mean socially awkward or tactless.

clue.text: Chicken shed emitting quiet bird sound

indicators.note: emitting means sending out, so this letter leaves the word for the shed

parts.note: a coop is a hen house
P is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A henhouse gives off a soft clucking noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A coo is the soft murmuring call made by doves and pigeons.

clue.text: Severe rain and storms surrounding company

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing on all sides, so the shuffled letters close around the next piece
storms throw things into turmoil, so the preceding words are thrown into a new order

parts.note: seven letters taken as written for the shuffle
standard abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Harsh weather of rain and storms engulfs a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storms' looks like part of the weather picture, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Draconian means excessively harsh, after Draco, the Athenian lawgiver whose laws were notoriously severe.

clue.text: Certain European flag over top of hall

parts.note: a flag is a type of iris plant, the yellow flag

indicators.note: the top is the uppermost part, so only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A national banner flies above the town hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' suggests a banner, but here it is the plant: the yellow flag is a wild iris. In a down clue, 'over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish describes someone from Ireland, so it names one particular kind of European.

clue.text: Consider flirting with detective at university

parts.note: a private eye is a detective
to be up is to be in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A student wonders about chatting up a police investigator on campus.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye up someone is a British idiom for looking at them with romantic or sexual interest.

clue.text: Drink up, finding mate

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, so the word is turned around

parts.note: to lap is to drink with the tongue, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Someone finishes their drink and finds a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Mate and pal are both informal words for a friend.

clue.text: Dishonourable recording about a good-looking person

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes round the next letter

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc
taken as written
a dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: A disreputable record has been made about a handsome star.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad is a man who behaves dishonourably, so caddish describes that kind of ungentlemanly conduct.

clue.text: Dicky hated milder setting for fantasy novels

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for faulty or unsound, so the letters that follow are out of order

parts.note: eleven letters taken as written for the shuffle

explanation.surface: A man called Dicky detested something gentler as the backdrop for fantasy books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a man's name, but it is British slang for shaky or unreliable, as in a dicky heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle-earth is the imaginary world where Tolkien set The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings.
